client-type-listed.statement: Machine Tunnel is one of the client types an access policy rule can select, beside Zscaler Client Connector, Client Connector for VDI, Client Connector Partner, Branch Connector, Cloud Connector, Web Browser, Internet & SaaS Service Edge and Extranet.

quotes: The available client types are Zscaler Client Connector, Client Connector for VDI, Client Connector Partner, Branch Connector, Cloud Connector, Machine Tunnel, Web Browser, Internet & SaaS Service Edge, or Extranet.

wire-labels.statement: The SDK's client types test expects the clientTypes endpoint to label `zpn_client_type_machine_tunnel` as Machine Tunnel and `zpn_client_type_zapp` as Client Connector.

client-types-or.statement: When a rule selects more than one client type, Private Access combines them with OR.

quotes: If you added multiple client types to the policy rule, Private Access uses an OR Boolean operator between them.
evidence.after: Machine Tunnel: To learn more, see About Machine Tunnels.

machine-tunnel-needs-own-rule.statement: An access rule that selects only the Client Connector client type does not select Machine Tunnel, so a machine tunnel session is covered only by a rule that selects Machine Tunnel; a session no rule covers meets the default Block Access outcome.
machine-tunnel-needs-own-rule.conditions: Chain of evidence: the console lists Client Connector and Machine Tunnel as separate client types and says nothing of one standing in for the other.

client-forwarding-meaning.statement: Client forwarding policy rules define when application requests are forwarded to Private Access from Zscaler Client Connector; with no matching rule the application is implicitly set to Forward to Private Access.

quotes: Client forwarding policy rules allow you to create rules that define when application requests are forwarded to Private Access from the Zscaler Client Connector.
For client forwarding policy, access to the application is implicitly set to Forward to Private Access.

forwarding-rule-accepts.statement: The provider documents `zpn_client_type_machine_tunnel` as a `CLIENT_TYPE` value for the v1 forwarding rule.

redirection-client-types.statement: Redirection policy rules set criteria for preferring Private Service Edges over Public Service Edges for Private Access. The Python SDK's add_redirection_rule_v2 helper accepts exactly five client type values: edge connector, branch connector, machine tunnel, zapp and zapp partner.

quotes: Redirection policy rules allow you to set criteria for preferring Private Service Edges for Private Access over Public Service Edges for Private Access.

v2-docs-omit-machine-tunnel.summary: The provider's v2 forwarding rule document leaves `zpn_client_type_machine_tunnel` out of its CLIENT_TYPE value list, while the provider's v2 validation accepts it and the v1 document lists it.

positions.says: The v2 forwarding rule CLIENT_TYPE values are listed without machine tunnel (and with a misspelt `zpn_client_type_zappl`).

v2-docs-omit-machine-tunnel.impact: A reader of the v2 document would conclude machine tunnel cannot be selected in a v2 forwarding rule, which the provider's own validation contradicts.

order-forwarding-vs-access.title: Whether client forwarding policy for a machine tunnel is evaluated before access policy
order-forwarding-vs-access.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Forwarding Policy evaluates before Access Policy. A forwarding rule with client type zpn_client_type_machine_tunnel can be used to route machine-tunnel traffic to a specific Service Edge group, or to bypass ZPA entirely for certain destinations." The policies help defines client forwarding policy as deciding when requests are forwarded to Private Access, not as routing to a Service Edge group, and gives no evaluation order against access policy. Confirm the order and the available actions in a scratch tenant.
